subject: Intermittent streaming lag — mitigation steps and post-incident check-in
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@pollenai.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@pollenai.com
Date: 2028-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent lag on streaming chat (June 14)

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

We started seeing elevated end-to-end latency for our web chat between 08:40–09:05 PT this morning. The client reports that tokens arrive in larger, uneven bursts rather than a steady stream, and some sessions hit a 6–8s per-chunk delay which causes our typing indicator to freeze.

Impact: ~7% of active chat sessions during the window, primarily west-coast users. No message drops, but UX is significantly degraded.

We've attached a short trace and a CSV of sampled RTTs. Can you confirm whether this maps to any maintenance or new rollout on your side? If not, what short-term changes would you recommend on our client to reduce perceived lag while you investigate?

Thanks — Olivia
Olivia Grant
Head of Platform, Pollen AI

Attachments: pollen_incident_timeline.pdf (3 pages, timeline), streaming_metrics_snapshot.csv (sampled RTTs)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@pollenai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-14T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent lag on streaming chat (June 14)

Olivia — thanks for the signal and the attachments. We're seeing the same spike in our edge telemetry for the US-west shard during that window. No planned maintenance was scheduled.

Short answers up front:
- We're routing immediate traffic to a healthy shard to reduce impact for sessions that can tolerate a brief reconnect.
- Engineering is triaging root cause (observed increased queuing and occasional KV-cache thrashing).

Immediate mitigations you can apply client-side (quick wins):
1) If you can accept slightly higher latency on full responses, switch to non-streaming / polling for high-risk sessions for 10–30 minutes.
2) Reduce your client request slice size (truncate max_response_tokens by 20–30%) to reduce per-token work and smooth pacing.
3) Implement a 500–700ms reconnect-backoff when chunk pacing pauses; this avoids waiting for long token gaps.

I'll keep you posted with a targeted engineering update in ~45–60 minutes.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ops_team@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: FW: triage notes — west-us streaming burst (internal)

Status update from infra: we saw an increase in the per-request scheduling latency at the runtime layer between 08:37–09:02 PT. Key observations:
- Burst of long-context requests (avg seq_len + 40%) caused temporary KV cache churn on a subset of GPU hosts.
- The scheduler's burst-burst heuristic didn't drain sufficiently fast because concurrent streams held long KV lifetimes.
- No model corruption; no token loss. Throughput dropped due to head-of-line blocking on a handful of hosts.

Actions taken (already applied):
- Temporary rate-limits enforced on the affected host pool and automatic soft-routing enabled to route new sessions to a warm standby pool.
- Increased KV cache TTL for the active pool to reduce thrash while we stabilize.
- Added an emergency short-circuit to fall back streaming requests to a non-streaming multi-chunk response on the affected hosts.

Next: full postmortem scheduled; we'll capture the trace and release a short remediation playbook for customers.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: reroute_playbook_v1.md
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@pollenai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: mitigation checklist & recommended client changes

Hi Olivia — following Ben's notes, here's a concise checklist you can use as an immediate operational playbook. We've included low-friction changes and one configuration you should avoid for now.

Short-term (apply immediately):
- Client-side fallbacks
  * If your app has a degraded-UX mode, enable non-streaming (single payload) for affected users for up to 30 minutes. This reduces head-of-line blocking on our side.
  * Add a lightweight pacing monitor: if no chunk arrives within 600ms, surface a soft spinner and attempt a single, short reconnect (no more than 700ms).
- Request shaping
  * Reduce max_tokens by 25% for interactive sessions during peak windows.
  * Avoid long multi-turn context sends; instead, send only the last 3 turns for streaming during the mitigation window.
- Routing & retries
  * If you observe repeated chunk gaps, retry the request via our non-streaming endpoint (/v1/completions with streaming disabled) and include X-Request-Reason: pacing-fallback header so we can tag the session for post-incident correlation.

Configuration to avoid right now:
- Do not blanket-enable aggressive client-side retries on chunk gaps (e.g., retry every 200ms). That magnifies load spikes and can worsen thrash.

We're prepping a short status note and a timeline for you; Ben's team will share the postmortem artifact and the exact host IDs. Please let us know whether you'd like Redwood to enable a temporary traffic pin to a specific warm pool while you apply client changes — we can coordinate a brief maintenance window.

Best — Laura
Laura Bennett
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@pollenai.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-16T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: mitigation checklist & recommended client changes

Thanks — the checklist is clear and actionable. We've toggled interactive sessions to polling for a small percentage of users and reduced max_tokens for mobile clients. Early telemetry shows a visible reduction in perceived lag.

Two quick asks:
1) Can you share the postmortem and the list of host IDs involved so our SREs can reconcile with our traces?
2) We'd appreciate a short, customer-ready summary we can share with our product team explaining what happened and the mitigations Redwood applied.

Olivia
